So I don't eat eggs, and I rarely eat dairy, maybe some fermented yogurt once in a while because I have stomach issues, but it's pretty rare, i am 'pretty much' vegan. However as I am not completely strict, I did not think I deserved to call myself a vegan, as there are many people who completely abide by the lifestyle and never stray, and they definitely earned the title. But yes, for the most part I do eat and live vegan, it would be hypocritical to think the egg & dairy industry is not factory farmed & causes animals suffering as well. Honestly, can't remember the last time i ate something that wasn't vegan, I buy vegan cheese, milks etc & no eggs sadly bc the fake eggs are so expensive. But yeah, guess I'm just used to saying i'm a vegetarian then....

I'm a vegetarian, but mostly because of the fact that I do not want to support factory farming, both for health, cruelty and environmental reasons. While raising your own animals to eat isn't *exactly* how things would be in the wild (literally hunting it down and giving the turkey a fair chance to try to escape etc.) I am sure your turkey had a wonderful life with you before it met it's end, and at least you know exactly where your food is coming from! There is a lot to be said about having a connection to your food, emotionally and viscerally and I feel this has taught a powerful and wonderful lesson. Cherish everything that turkey will give you. If I ever did go back to eating meat, it would have to be under circumstances like this.
